designation: IN THE COURT OF DISTRICT & SESSIONS JUDGE
jurisdictionNote: District-level criminal and civil courts in Uttarakhand, governed by the Uttar Pradesh Civil Courts Act, 1887 (as adapted by Uttarakhand on State formation in 2000) read with the Allahabad/Nainital High Court Rules. Sessions courts try offences punishable with imprisonment exceeding 7 years. Uttarakhand presently comprises 13 revenue districts spread across the Garhwal and Kumaon divisions and the subordinate judiciary is supervised by the High Court of Uttarakhand at Nainital. Hindi is the official language of the State subordinate courts under the Uttarakhand Official Language Act, 2000.

party_designation.state: State of Uttarakhand through the Principal Secretary, Home Department, Government of Uttarakhand, Dehradun

prayer_language.opening: It is, therefore, most respectfully prayed that this Hon'ble Court may graciously be pleased to:
prayer_language.closing: And for this act of kindness, the petitioner shall, as in duty bound, ever pray.

verification_format:
I, {deponent_name}, {designation}, do hereby solemnly verify and declare that the contents of paragraphs ___ to ___ of the above petition are true to my personal knowledge and the contents of paragraphs ___ to ___ are based on information received and legal advice tendered, which I believe to be true. Nothing material has been concealed therefrom.

Verified at {place} on this {date}.

DEPONENT
localRules: Hindi is the official language of the Uttarakhand subordinate courts under the Uttarakhand Official Language Act, 2000; pleadings before the Uttarakhand High Court at Nainital are in English. District court pleadings may be filed in Hindi (Devanagari) with English translation where required.
Bail applications under S.483 BNSS (formerly S.439 CrPC) before the Sessions Court must disclose any prior rejection by a Magistrate or co-ordinate court.
Anticipatory bail applications (S.482 BNSS) must be accompanied by an affidavit, certified copy of the FIR and grounds of apprehension.
Vakalatnama in the form prescribed under the Uttarakhand High Court Rules to be filed at the first instance with requisite court-fee stamp.
All civil pleadings to be paginated, indexed and accompanied by a list of documents under Order VII / Order VIII CPC.
Court-fee under the Court-Fees Act, 1870 as in force in Uttarakhand with State amendments; ad valorem fee structure applies to civil suits.
Atrocities (SC/ST), POCSO and NDPS cases are tried by designated Special Courts notified by the State Government — typically the District & Sessions Judge at the district headquarters.
Designated Special Courts also exist for offences under the Uttarakhand (Uttar Pradesh Zamindari Abolition and Land Reforms Act, 1950 as adapted) and revenue laws where notified.

Hill districts (Uttarkashi, Chamoli, Rudraprayag, Pithoragarh, Bageshwar, Champawat, Tehri Garhwal, Pauri Garhwal, Almora) follow seasonal court calendars; record-of-rights and revenue forums under the Uttar Pradesh Land Revenue Act, 1901 (as adapted) interface frequently with civil jurisdiction.

Dehradun (state capital), Haridwar and Nainital host the principal district court establishments; the Uttarakhand High Court sits at Nainital with a proposed permanent seat at Gairsain under consideration.
e_filing_note: e-Filing is operational at Dehradun, Haridwar and Nainital via the eCourts portal; not yet mandatory state-wide.
